# How a release works

*customers.riskmandate.ai · operations · written at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20) · CC BY 4.0*

Every push to `dev` is a release. There is no build step at deploy time: the committed tree is the deployed tree, and seven small generators keep the parts that must agree in agreement. One pipeline validates, tags, deploys and then checks that the live site is serving what was pushed.

## The version

- The version lives in one file, `admin/build/version.txt`, as `X.Y.Z` with no `v`.
- Every push to `dev` bumps the minor (`0.1.0` to `0.2.0`). A patch (`0.2.1`) is for a same-day fix. A major `.0.0` is deliberate and rare.
- The release commit's subject is `site vX.Y.Z : <what>`, with the same version. CI anchors on the newest commit whose subject has that shape, not on HEAD, because a merge commit may sit on top.
- `data/versions.json` gets a new first row: version, date, title, notes. The title is the `<what>` of the subject. The note says what changed and why, in words a reader can act on.
- The version is repeated by the generators into every page badge, every markdown twin, `llms.txt`, `llms-full.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and the release table. Check 1 of the gate fails on any disagreement.

## The steps, locally

```
# 1. edit content; edit data/customers.json, data/reality.json as the facts change
python3 admin/build/release.py --version X.Y.Z --kind feature --title "<what>" --notes "<why>"
#    which does: bump version.txt and versions.json; gate.py --build; commit "site vX.Y.Z : <what>"; push dev; verify live
# or by hand:
python3 admin/build/gate.py --build      # regenerate everything, then run the whole gate
git add -A
git commit -m "site vX.Y.Z : <what>"
git push -u origin dev                   # or open a pull request to dev from claude/<description>-<session-id>
```

`gate.py --build` runs the generators in order (customers, reality, docs, the review tools, chrome, versions, twins, llms), then runs them again with `--check`, then `node admin/build/validate.js`, then `python3 -m pytest tests/build/ -q`, then `node --test tests/unit/**/*.test.js`. `gate.py` without `--build` runs the same list in check mode only, which is exactly what CI does.

## The steps, in CI (`.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`)

| Job | When | Does | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| `validate` | every push to `dev` or `main`, every pull request to either, manual dispatch | `python3 admin/build/gate.py` | nothing is tagged or deployed |
| `tag-release` | push to `dev` only | `admin/build/tag_release.py`: version.txt equals the newest `site vX.Y.Z` subject; the version is the next minor, a patch or a major `.0.0` after the newest tag; backfills missing historical tags; pushes `refs/tags/vX.Y.Z` | no deploy |
| `deploy` | any push or dispatch, never a pull request | `admin/build/assemble_site.py` copies the tree minus `.git`, `.github`, `tests/unit`, `node_modules` into `_site/`; upload and deploy to GitHub Pages | the previous version stays live |
| `verify-live` | after deploy | `admin/build/verify_live.py` polls `https://customers.riskmandate.ai/admin/build/version.txt` and the home page badge with a cache-buster until both equal the version, for up to ten minutes | the run is red; the site may be stale |

A push to `main` deploys without tagging: `main` is promoted from `dev` and is the fallback. Both branches deploy to the one Pages site of this repository, so whichever pushed last is what the host serves; `main` is promoted only to a version `dev` already released.

## Green does not mean live

A sibling site once pushed two releases that reported success and never reached anyone, because the Pages deploy job died downloading its own action. The `verify-live` job exists for that reason: the release is not done until the origin answers with the new version. When `verify-live` is red and `deploy` is green, the usual causes are the domain not yet pointing at Pages (see [needs.md](needs.md)), Pages not yet enabled for the repository with the custom domain, or a transient `429` on an action download, which a re-run fixes. The first release of this site, v0.1.0, was pushed before the DNS record existed, so its `verify-live` is expected red until the lead's step is done; the re-run is the lead's.

## The eight checks of the gate

See `/admin/` on the site or the header of `admin/build/validate.js`. The rule for the leak tripwire is worth repeating: the fix for a trip is always a redaction, never a wider pattern. The rule for the house words is riskmandate.ai's: the verbatim documents are exempt and nothing else is.

## Backfilling tags

`tag_release.py` tags every historical release commit that has no tag, oldest first, then pushes all the new tags. A tag that already points at its release commit is left alone. A tag that points elsewhere fails the job: tags are never moved.

# The team

*customers.riskmandate.ai · who does what, as files · written at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20) · in the shape of the sgit.ai team section and the riskmandate.ai team page · CC BY 4.0*

Three roles fill every seat at this stage, held by one person and one agent. Each role is one file with the rules it enforces and the mistake behind each rule, so that a new agent can read this page and one role and begin. The board of work is [board.md](board.md), the work as files with a status line each, and [needs.md](../docs/ops/needs.md), the asks back to the person. Neither lives in a vault yet; if the board outgrows a file, it moves to a vault of its own and this page says where.

| Role | Held by | Decides |
|---|---|---|
| [Project lead](roles/project-lead.md) | Dinis Cruz | What ships next, what the brief means where it is ambiguous, who is in the batch and under what handle, the credit, everything that needs a human account (DNS, Pages, the meter, the list) |
| [Build agent](roles/build-agent.md) | A Claude Code session, one at a time | Everything else, within the rules its role file lists, recording each departure from the brief in the corrections file |
| [Customer follow-up](roles/customer-follow-up.md) | The lead, for the first batch; an agent drafts | The daily contact with each customer, the three questions, and what is recorded on the customer page |

The agents that make riskmandate.ai have behaviour policies of their own on [its team page](https://riskmandate.ai/team/); this site's build agent is a Claude Code session of the same kind and will get one as part of the record *the-agents* in the batch. Other teams review the work and the review is published with the reply; the first review this site expects is the sgit.ai site team's, against its repository rules.

# The board

*customers.riskmandate.ai · the work as files · written at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20) · CC BY 4.0*

One line per piece of work, with a status: `open`, `building`, `done vX.Y.Z`, or `waits on <who>`. A row moves because the thing happened, by a release; nothing is dragged. The asks that only a person can do are in [needs.md](../docs/ops/needs.md) and are not repeated here.

| # | Work | Status |
|---|---|---|
| B1 | The site, from the brief: pipeline, gate, chrome, the content pages, the brief in full, the corrections file, reality, the team, the review folder's intent half | done v0.1.0 |

| B3 | The list of the ten agents, one line each, with the nearest published shape | waits on the lead (needs 10) |
| B4 | The grant of one Claude Code session, measured with MAP-A-GRANT.md: the lead's step S2 | open |
| B5 | The meter wired to this host, and the credit accounts for the batch | waits on the lead (needs 5, 6) |

| B8 | The form for the next batch, on this site | waits on the lead (needs 7) |
| B9 | The derived half of the review folder, and review/self/ | open; from the next change, delta first |
| B10 | The behaviour policy of this site's build agent, in the riskmandate.ai team grammar | open |

# Role: build agent

*customers.riskmandate.ai · the Claude Code session · written at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20) · CC BY 4.0*

The session that builds the site from the brief, one release at a time, under the rules below. It never pushes a release that fails the gate, never writes a secret or a contact detail into the tree, and never describes a thing in the present tense before `data/reality.json` says shipped.

## Rules this role enforces, and the mistake behind each

| Rule | The mistake it came from |
|---|---|
| Run `python3 admin/build/gate.py --build` before every commit; CI runs the same command. | A sibling site shipped two releases that reported success and never reached anyone; the gate and verify-live exist for that reason. |
| Every number on a page is generated from a file or dated with the file it came from. | nfrs.sgit.ai's rule: an index maintained by hand becomes a lie on a schedule. The counts, the batch table and reality are written by scripts. |
| Never "ADP", never "the policy" alone, no score on a behaviour policy, "steps" not "rungs", British English. | riskmandate.ai's rules, each with a reason on its own CLAUDE.md; the gate enforces them here, and the verbatim brief and memo are exempt. |
| No contact details in any file; the gate fails on anything contact-shaped in the customer records. | The brief's "no customer is named"; the repository is public. |
| When the brief is wrong, record it in BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md and carry on; never edit the brief or the memo. | The brief is the one that was accepted; the memo is the one that was said. |
| When something needs a human, write exactly what, as a command, in needs.md, and continue with what does not depend on it. | A step that lives in a chat does not get done. |
| The fix for a tripwire hit is a redaction, never a wider pattern. | A wider pattern hides the next real key. |
| No em-dashes in prose the session writes; the gate says so as an advisory. | The house prose rule; the verbatim documents are exempt. |
| A release is `site vX.Y.Z : what`, the version bumped, the note saying what changed and why. | "UI improvements" tells a reader nothing; the release history is the repository's memory. |

## Starting prompt

"Read README.md, docs/ops/release.md, docs/brief/BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md and team/board.md. Continue from the first open row on the board that does not wait on the lead. Every release is `site vX.Y.Z : what` with the minor bumped and a `Kind:` trailer."

# Role: customer follow-up

*customers.riskmandate.ai · held by the lead for the first batch; an agent drafts · written at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20) · CC BY 4.0*

The daily contact with each customer. Asks three things, as often as daily if that helps: what they did, what got in the way, what is next. Records the answers on the customer page in summary and keeps the rest with the lead. The pattern is the newsroom's: an agent drafts, a person reads and sends, and nothing goes out that a person has not seen.

## Rules this role enforces, and the mistake behind each

| Rule | The mistake it came from |
|---|---|
| Three questions, a line each is plenty; "nothing, I was busy" is a fine answer and goes in the log. | A follow-up that reads as a form gets no reply; Paul Graham's attentiveness is a person asking, not a survey. |
| The log on the customer page is the summary; names of systems, the contents of a grant or a mandate, and anything the customer did not want public stay with the lead. | The brief: nothing is published without their yes, and the default is no. |
| The second answer, what got in the way, is read against the three questions on the learning page, and a pattern across customers becomes a finding with its count. | A finding typed before it was counted is a guess; the learning page's table starts empty on purpose. |
| A customer who has not replied is asked again, not marked. | A status that says "stalled" is a judgement; the log records dates and the ladder records steps. |
| The follow-up names the step the customer is on and links their page, so they can see what the site says about them. | A page about a person that the person has not seen is a page they cannot correct. |

## The message

The template is on [the follow-up page](../../follow-up/index.md). An agent fills `{first name}`, `{step}` and `{id}` from the private list and the customer record; a person sends it from agent@riskmandate.ai.

## Starting prompt

"For each customer in data/customers.json whose status is not example, draft today's follow-up from the template, with the step they are on and the link to their page, and put the drafts where the lead reads them. Do not send."


==============================================================================
source: /team/roles/project-lead.md
==============================================================================

# Role: project lead

*customers.riskmandate.ai · Dinis Cruz · written at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20) · CC BY 4.0*

The person. Speaks or writes the brief; an agent drafts; the person accepts. Decides who is in the batch and under what handle, what the credit is, what the brief means where it is ambiguous, and everything that needs a human account.

## Rules this role enforces, and the mistake behind each

| Rule | The mistake it came from |
|---|---|
| A brief is the person's words, in either hand, and is published in full before the work starts. | A site built from a conversation nobody can read cannot be checked against anything but itself; the repository rules say so and the newsroom's briefs are the pattern. |
| Nobody is listed as a customer without their yes, and the default is no. | The brief's own rule, "no customer is named"; the memo named the first users, and C2 in the corrections says how that was reconciled. |
| A customer's private details never enter the repository; the lead holds them. | The repository is public and every file in it is deployed; a leak is an incident, not a typo. |
| Every ask that needs a human is written as a command in needs.md, and the lead does it or says why not. | The sibling sites' DNS and Pages steps sat undone because they were in a chat, not on a page. |
| The lead reads the correction above the mistake, never edits the brief to match. | A corrected brief would no longer be the one that was accepted. |

## Starting prompt

"Read the start-here page as a customer would and say where it is hard to understand. Then read needs.md and do the first open item or say why not."

# Corrections to the review brief, for this repository

*customers.riskmandate.ai · started at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20) · CC BY 4.0*

The review brief is [Code review graphs in the repository](https://sgit.ai/docs/briefs/code-review-graphs-in-the-repository.html), on sgit.ai. Where this repository does not follow it, the entry is here, dated, with the reason.

## R1. Only the intent half exists at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20)

The brief asks a new repository to build the whole folder before its first source file. This repository built the intent half (stories, rules, examples, anchored to the brief and the memo), a validator and a static rendering, and shipped the site. The derived half, the join, the change files, the web-component navigator and `self/` are proposed, recorded in `data/reality.json` as *site.review-derived*. Reason: the site had to exist on the day the brief was accepted; a review folder for a site that does not exist reviews nothing. The next change starts the derived half, delta first.

## R2. The brief's headings are not numbered (2026-10-20)

The review brief's `sections.json` keys sections by number. The newsroom article that is this site's brief has prose headings with no numbers, so `tools/sections.py` keys them by the heading's slug, which is also the anchor on the rendered page. The memo document is anchored the same way, and both are in one `sections.json` under `docs`.

## R3. The navigator is a page, not components (2026-10-20)

The brief asks for a navigator built as web components in the coding.sgit.ai shape. `review/index.html` is a static page rendered by `tools/render.py`, with the same links a navigator would have (every node to its section of the brief and to the page it lands on), and no script. The components come with the derived half.

source: /review/README.md

# review/: the brief as intent, and what is not derived yet

*customers.riskmandate.ai · written at v0.1.0 (2026-10-20) · CC BY 4.0*

The sgit.ai repository rules ask every repository to carry a review folder from its first commit, in the shape of [Code review graphs in the repository](https://sgit.ai/docs/briefs/code-review-graphs-in-the-repository.html): the intent written top down from the brief, the code derived bottom up from the syntax tree by parsers, the join between the two with a coverage figure, every commit read upwards, a navigator built as web components, and `self/` for the tools. This folder has the first of those and says so.

## What is here

- `intent/stories.json`: the brief and the memo as stories, rules and examples, written by the build session on 2026-10-20, each node carrying the document and the heading it came from. Not yet accepted by a person; the lead accepts by a release that sets `accepted_by`.
- `intent/sections.json`: every heading of the brief and the memo with the anchor the rendered page gives it, generated by `tools/sections.py`, so every source resolves to a place a reader can click.
- `tools/validate_review.py`: the shape checks; it runs in the gate. `tools/render.py` renders the intent into [the review page](index.html), static HTML with no script.
- [BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md](BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md): where the review brief was not followed, and why.

## What is not here

The derived half: `graph/`, `join/`, `changes/`, `streams/`, `checks/`, the navigator as web components, and `self/`. The reality file carries it as *site.review-derived*, proposed. The plan is the repository rules' own: from the next change, delta first, letting the graph grow along the paths people walk.

## Regenerate and check

```
python3 review/tools/sections.py             # the headings of the brief and the memo, with anchors
python3 review/tools/validate_review.py      # every source resolves; every surface is a page; ids unique
python3 review/tools/render.py               # the review page
```
